title: Why it happened and what it's for
title_target: Akibat hujan deras, Kali Wangi meluap
goal: Explain causes, results and purposes the way reports and proposals do — *akibat*, *sehingga*, *oleh karena itu*, *maka*, *agar*, *demi* — and keep apart the two that learners confuse most: *sehingga* (result) and *agar* (purpose).
bekal: give a cause with *karena*, *akibat*, *berkat* or *gara-gara*, choosing the right tone
state a result with *sehingga*, *oleh karena itu* and *maka*
state a purpose with *untuk*, *agar/supaya* and *demi*, and never mix it up with a result

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Laporan kerusakan banjir
dialogs.intro: Mid-April 2028. After two days of heavy rain, the little river that runs past Sumberwangi has burst its banks again, far worse than in March. On Saturday morning Pak Harun and Sarah sit in the village hall to write the damage report for the regional disaster agency.

lines.speaker: Harun:
lines.text: Mbak Sarah, laporan untuk BPBD harus kita kirim hari ini agar bantuan cepat turun.
lines.id: Sarah, we have to send the report to the disaster agency today so that help comes quickly.
lines.literal: Miss Sarah, report for BPBD must we send day this so-that aid fast descend.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Baik, Pak. Saya mulai dengan penyebabnya: hujan deras selama dua hari.
lines.id: All right. I'll start with the cause: two days of heavy rain.
lines.literal: good, sir. I start with cause-its: rain heavy during two day.

lines.speaker: Harun:
lines.text: Betul. Akibat hujan deras itu, Kali Wangi meluap pada Kamis malam.
lines.id: Right. As a result of that heavy rain, the Wangi river overflowed on Thursday night.
lines.literal: correct. result rain heavy that, River Wangi overflow on Thursday night.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Air masuk ke rumah warga sehingga tiga homestay terendam.
lines.id: Water got into people's houses, so that three homestays were flooded.
lines.literal: water enter to house resident so-that three homestay submerged.

lines.speaker: Harun:
lines.text: Tulis juga: lima hektare sawah rusak. Oleh karena itu, panen bulan depan terancam gagal.
lines.id: Put this too: five hectares of rice fields were damaged. Therefore next month's harvest is at risk of failing.
lines.literal: write also: five hectare rice-field damaged. by because that, harvest month front threatened fail.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Apakah jumlah kerugiannya perlu kita sebutkan?
lines.id: Do we need to state the amount of the losses?
lines.literal: whether amount loss-the need we mention?

lines.speaker: Harun:
lines.text: Perlu. Kerugian diperkirakan sekitar sembilan puluh juta rupiah.
lines.id: We do. The losses are estimated at about ninety million rupiah.
lines.literal: need. loss be-estimated around nine ten million rupiah.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Lalu bantuan apa saja yang kita minta, Pak?
lines.id: And what kind of help are we asking for?
lines.literal: then aid what just that we ask, sir?

lines.speaker: Harun:
lines.text: Pertama, pompa untuk menyedot sisa air. Kedua, semen dan pasir untuk perbaikan rumah.
lines.id: First, pumps to suck out the remaining water. Second, cement and sand to repair the houses.
lines.literal: first, pump for suck remainder water. second, cement and sand for repair house.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Ketiga?
lines.id: And third?
lines.literal: third?

lines.speaker: Harun:
lines.text: Karung pasir, demi mencegah banjir berikutnya. Musim hujan belum selesai.
lines.id: Sandbags, to prevent the next flood. The rainy season isn't over.
lines.literal: sack sand, for-the-sake-of prevent flood next. season rain not-yet finish.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Saya tambahkan satu kalimat: “Jika bantuan terlambat, maka warga akan sulit memulihkan usaha homestay.”
lines.id: I'll add one sentence: “If help is delayed, residents will find it hard to restore their homestay businesses.”
lines.literal: I add one sentence: if aid late, then residents will difficult restore business homestay.

lines.speaker: Harun:
lines.text: Bagus. Untuk lampiran, pakai foto yang diambil Yoga kemarin.
lines.id: Good. For the attachments, use the photos Yoga took yesterday.
lines.literal: good. for attachment, use photo that be-taken Yoga yesterday.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Sudah saya lampirkan. Laporannya tinggal Bapak tanda tangani.
lines.id: I've attached them. The report just needs your signature.
lines.literal: already I attach. report-the remain you sign.

notes: **BPBD** — *Badan Penanggulangan Bencana Daerah*, the regional disaster management agency; each regency has one, and the national body is BNPB. Reports to it are written in a plain, formal style: dates, causes, figures, requests.

**Akibat hujan deras itu** — *akibat* (“as a result of”) introduces a cause whose outcome is bad. It is the word of news reports and insurance forms: *akibat kecelakaan*, *akibat banjir*. For a good outcome, use *berkat* (“thanks to”).

**Sehingga tiga homestay terendam** — *sehingga* introduces the **result**: “so that / with the result that”. It is not purpose. The rain did not *want* to flood the homestays; it just did. The grammar box shows why this matters.
**Oleh karena itu** — “therefore”, literally “by because of that”. It opens a new sentence and belongs to formal speech and writing. In conversation people say *jadi* or *makanya*.

**Demi mencegah banjir berikutnya** — *demi* is “for the sake of”, stronger and more solemn than *untuk*. It suits a goal you care about: *demi keselamatan warga*, *demi anak-anak*. Using it for sandbags gives Pak Harun's request a little extra weight.

**Tinggal Bapak tanda tangani** — *tinggal* (“remain”) means “all that's left is…”. Combined with the pronoun passive it makes a tidy, polite hand-over: *tinggal Bapak cek*, *tinggal Ibu bayar*. Note the spelling *hektare*, which is the standard form, though *hektar* is common too.

grammars.title: Cause: karena, sebab, akibat, berkat, gara-gara
body: All of these introduce a cause, but they carry different feelings about the outcome and belong to different registers.
after: ⚠️ *Berkat* and *akibat* are not interchangeable. *Berkat banjir, …* sounds as if you are grateful for the flood.
*Akibat* is also a noun: *akibatnya* (“as a result”, “the consequence”) opens a sentence in speech and writing: *Akibatnya, tiga homestay terendam.*

grammars.title: Result: sehingga, oleh karena itu, maka, jadi
body: These introduce what followed. The first joins two clauses in one sentence; the others usually open a new sentence or clause.
after: ⚠️ *Karena… maka…* in one sentence is a common error in formal Indonesian: *Karena hujan, maka acara dibatalkan* has one conjunction too many. Write either *Karena hujan, acara dibatalkan* or *Hujan turun. Oleh karena itu, acara dibatalkan.*
*Maka* after *jika* or *apabila* is accepted and very common in official texts. In conversation it disappears altogether.

dialogs.title: Second dialogue — Mencari donatur
dialogs.intro: Ten days later, in a hotel meeting room in Yogyakarta. Ibu Anggraini, who owns a small hotel group and runs its community programme, has agreed to hear Sarah's pitch for a flood wall.

lines.speaker: Anggraini:
lines.text: Jadi, dana yang Mbak butuhkan berapa, dan untuk apa?
lines.id: So how much money do you need, and what for?
lines.literal: so, fund that Miss need how-much, and for what?

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Seratus lima puluh juta, Bu, untuk membangun tanggul agar banjir tidak terulang.
lines.id: A hundred and fifty million, to build a flood wall so the flooding doesn't happen again.
lines.literal: one-hundred five ten million, madam, for build embankment so-that flood not be-repeated.

lines.speaker: Anggraini:
lines.text: Kenapa kami harus membantu Sumberwangi, bukan desa lain?
lines.id: Why should we help Sumberwangi rather than another village?
lines.literal: why we must help Sumberwangi, not village other?

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Karena desa ini sudah punya bukti. Berkat homestay, pendapatan warga sudah mulai naik.
lines.id: Because this village has already proved itself. Thanks to the homestays, residents' income has already started to rise.
lines.literal: because village this already have proof. thanks-to homestay, income resident already start rise.

lines.speaker: Anggraini:
lines.text: Lalu kalau banjir datang lagi?
lines.id: And if the flood comes again?
lines.literal: then if flood come again?

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Semua itu bisa hilang. Oleh karena itu, tanggul ini bukan biaya, melainkan investasi.
lines.id: All of that could be lost. That's why this wall is not a cost but an investment.
lines.literal: all that can lost. by because that, embankment this not cost, but-rather investment.

lines.speaker: Anggraini:
lines.text: Kalimat yang bagus. Tapi apa yang kami dapat?
lines.id: Nicely put. But what do we get out of it?
lines.literal: sentence that good. but what that we get?

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Nama perusahaan Ibu dicantumkan di papan desa, dan tamu hotel Ibu mendapat paket kunjungan khusus.
lines.id: Your company's name goes on the village signboard, and your hotel guests get a special visit package.
lines.literal: name company madam be-listed at board village, and guest hotel madam get package visit special.

lines.speaker: Anggraini:
lines.text: Menarik. Kirimkan proposal lengkapnya supaya bisa saya bawa ke rapat direksi.
lines.id: Interesting. Send me the full proposal so I can take it to the board meeting.
lines.literal: interesting. send proposal complete-the so-that can I bring to meeting directors.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Siap, Bu. Demi warga Sumberwangi, besok pagi proposalnya sudah di meja Ibu.
lines.id: Certainly. For the people of Sumberwangi, the proposal will be on your desk tomorrow morning.
lines.literal: ready, madam. for-sake-of residents Sumberwangi, tomorrow morning proposal-the already at desk madam.

notes: **Dana** is “funds”, the formal word for money set aside for a purpose: *dana desa* (village funds from the central budget), *dana bantuan*, *penggalangan dana* (fundraising). In everyday speech money is *uang* or *duit*.

**Agar banjir tidak terulang** — *agar* introduces a **purpose**, something wanted. *Terulang* is *ter-* in its “happen (again) by itself” sense: *jangan sampai terulang* (“it mustn't happen again”) is heard after every disaster.
**Berkat homestay** — Sarah switches from *akibat* to *berkat* the moment the news is good. Fundraising language in Indonesian, as in English, leans on proof: *bukti*, *data*, *hasil*.

**Bukan biaya, melainkan investasi** — *bukan… melainkan…* is “not… but rather…”, the formal way to correct or reframe. In speech *bukan… tapi…* does the same job. Use *melainkan* only after a negative with *bukan* or *tidak*.
**Dicantumkan** — from *cantum*, “to be listed, printed (on)”. Names of sponsors are *dicantumkan*; so are prices on a menu and conditions in a contract (*seperti yang tercantum*, “as stated”).
**Rapat direksi** — a meeting of the board of directors (*direksi*). Ibu Anggraini's *supaya bisa saya bawa* uses the pronoun passive inside a purpose clause: “so that it can be taken by me”.

grammars.title: Purpose: untuk, agar, supaya, demi, guna
body: Purpose words answer “what for?”. The main choice is whether a verb or a whole clause (with its own subject) follows.
after: ⚠️ The classic mix-up: *sehingga* is result, *agar/supaya* is purpose. *Kami bekerja keras sehingga proyeknya selesai* = we worked hard, and so it got finished. *Kami bekerja keras agar proyeknya selesai* = we worked hard in order to finish it. English “so that” can mean either, which is exactly why learners trip here.
*Untuk* can also be followed by a clause in speech (*untuk kita pakai*), but *agar* or *supaya* is cleaner whenever the clause has its own subject.

blocks.text: Floods, landslides and volcanic ash are part of life in Central Java, and the vocabulary appears in every regional newspaper each rainy season. These are the words you need to read a report — or help write one.
*Tidak ada korban jiwa* — “there were no fatalities” — is the sentence everyone waits for in a disaster report, and it is usually said early. *Jebol* means “burst through”, of walls, dams and nets.

items: *Akibat Hujan Deras, Ratusan Rumah di Magelang Terendam* — As a result of heavy rain, hundreds of homes in Magelang flooded.
*Warga Mengungsi, Jalan Provinsi Ditutup Sementara* — Residents evacuate, provincial road temporarily closed.
*Berkat Gotong Royong, Tanggul Jebol Diperbaiki dalam Sehari* — Thanks to community effort, burst embankment repaired in a day.

sections.title: From chat to report: one idea, three registers

blocks.text: The same logical link sounds very different in a WhatsApp message, in conversation and in a formal report. Knowing all three lets you understand everyone — and write the right one.

blocks.title: One event, three ways
items: 💬 *Gara-gara hujan, rumah Bu Ratna kebanjiran. Makanya kita perlu tanggul.*
*Karena hujan deras, rumah Bu Ratna kebanjiran. Jadi kita perlu tanggul.*
*Akibat hujan deras, rumah warga terendam. Oleh karena itu, diperlukan pembangunan tanggul.*

blocks.text: A good formal paragraph usually moves in this order: cause (*akibat…*), result (*sehingga…*), consequence for the future (*oleh karena itu…*), and request with its purpose (*…agar…*). Sarah's report follows that shape exactly, which is why it reads so clearly.
Cover the Indonesian column, read the English, and rebuild each sentence from memory.
